newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb sells Oral Care business to Conair.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb sells Oral Care business to Conair.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb Inc. said on Monday it has completed the sale of its Oral Care Division to Conair, a maker of personal care appliances, health and beauty products, kitchen appliances and telephones.

Bausch & Lomb did not disclose the sale price, but said it expects to take a one-time charge of $6.3 million, or 11 cents per share, in the third quarter for the sale, which is part of the company's strategy to focus on its core eye care business.
The Rochester, N.Y.-based company in January announced its intention to exit the Oral Care business.

The division has sold the Interplak line of power toothbrushes for plaque removal since 1988, when Bausch & Lomb acquired Dental Research Corp., the creator of Interplak. The division accounts for less than 3 percent of Bausch & Lomb's total revenues.

Conair, a privately held company based in East Windsor, N.J., makes Cuisinart food processors, Jheri Redding shampoos and conditioners, Conair hairdryers and curling irons, and the Southwestern Bell Freedom Phone.
Bausch & Lomb's stock fell 12.5 cents to $37 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
